📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Six Tom Waits songs that were previously available only on vinyl have been added to streaming services to commemorate the 20th anniversary of the artist’s Orphans: Brawlers, Bawlers & Bastards box set. The EP, titled Orphans: Bonus, originally came out when the Orphans set got upgraded from CD to vinyl in 2009.

According to recent reports, the Orphans foundlings are a mix of originals, cover songs, and collaborations. Waits recorded the soulful, jazzy “Pray” with the Book of Knots, an avant-garde rock group also on his record label, Anti-. Another jazzy recording is Waits’ funky, piano-driven cover of Fats Waller’s “Crazy ‘Bout My Baby.” Meanwhile, he sings his rendition of Kurt Weill and Bertolt Brecht’s “The Cannon Song,” from The Threepenny Opera, to samples of huffing and puffing voices, a perfect backdrop to singing about eating hamburgers raw.

In a recent development, he sings his original, “Diamond in Your Mind,” to a lush backdrop of orchestral strings, fretless bass, and tambourine, which supports the chorus, “Always keep a diamond in your mind.” He wrote the song with songwriter (and his wife) Kathleen Brennan for Robert Wilson’s Woyzeck; Solomon Burke later recorded it. Waits wrote the EP’s penultimate track by himself. “No One Can Forgive Me but My Baby” is like a blues recitative set to percussion and sparse instrumentation as he begs for forgiveness. The album’s last song, “Mathie Grove,” is an old murder ballad that Waits sings a cappella.

According to recent reports, the original Orphans box set came out on three CDs. The first, Brawlers, contained harder blues and rock songs, while Bawlers featured ballads, and Bastards was more avant-garde. Among the tracks were songs written for soundtracks and several covers including Ramones’ “The Return of Jackie and Judy” and “Sea of Love.” “At the center of this record is my voice,” Waits commented on the box set at the time of its release. “I try my best to chug, stomp, weep, whisper, moan, wheeze, scat, blurt, rage, whine and seduce.” It was nominated for the Best Contemporary Folk Album Grammy. Trending Stories Marlon Jackson Reveals Stage 4 Prostate Cancer Diagnosis Selena Gomez Shares Her Reaction to Martin Short Ruining Her Wedding Cake Some Gamers Are Pissed That ‘GTA VI’ Makes Them Be Nice to Their Girlfriend Trump Got Played by Putin and Xi.

In April, Waits released his first latest music in 15 years, “Boots on the Ground,” a gruesome song protesting war that Waits he recorded with Massive Attack; the B side was a spoken-word piece called “The Fly.”.

He also recently contributed a rendition of the Pogues’ “Summer in Siam” to the tribute compilation, 20th Century Paddy – The Songs of Shane MacGowan. He gave Rolling Stone an exclusive statement about MacGowan for an article about the compilation: “His voice can sing about a well, and I’ll be sure to fall into it,” he wrote, “and sing about a factory wall, and I’m weary leaning and warily wooing that girl taking a drag off my smoke, and he can sing about a battle, and my head will be bloody and bandaged at the end of the song.… His songs come from the earth, the wind, the birds, and the bees, the gone and forgotten but for their songs.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • That’s why I drove the Hyundai Ioniq 9 Calligraphy Design for the second time this year — just to convince myself that there are better 3-row midsize SUVs out there.
  • But after another week behind the wheel, I can tell you firsthand that judging the Ioniq 9 by its cover is a mistake.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Quite frankly, the Hyundai Ioniq 9 gets a bad rap for the way it looks. In fact, I remarked in my 2026 Hyundai Ioniq 9 review that the design is an “odd mashup featuring a curvy front bumper with an even stranger-looking arched rear.” It’s one of the last SUVs I’d expect to win any beauty awards.

That’s why I drove the Hyundai Ioniq 9 Calligraphy Design for the second time this year — just to convince myself that there are better 3-row midsize SUVs out there. I’ve spent more time testing 3-row SUVs than any other vehicle type this year, with models like the Kia Telluride, Volvo XC90, Volkswagen Atlas, and Lucid Gravity getting my seal of approval.

But after another week behind the wheel, I can tell you firsthand that judging the Ioniq 9 by its cover is a mistake. Here’s what I realized.

Best long distance driving efficiency.

Best short distance driving efficiency.

It has been revealed that as with most vehicles, fuel economy and efficiency tend to dwindle over time — which is why I’m shocked that the Ioniq 9 is an exception. I was already impressed by the 3 mi/kWh average I got when I drove it last year, yet my second run delivered even better results.

In a recent development, across 130.5 miles of mixed driving, my second go-around with the Ioniq 9 yielded an impressive 3.3 mi/kWh. What surprised me even more was the substantial improvement in city driving, where I recorded a peak tally of 4.5 mi/kWh — up from my previous best of 3.8 mi/kWh.

Considering it’s marketed as a three-row family hauler, it’s remarkable that the Ioniq 9 can post numbers like this. That extra efficiency is critical, too: while this trim carries an EPA-estimated range of 311 miles, averaging 3.3 mi/kWh puts its real-world range closer to 363 miles.

I’ll admit I was harsh on the Hyundai Ioniq 9’s styling the first time around. While it certainly takes cues from the subcompact Hyundai Kona, I argued that it was an odd mashup that was confused about what aesthetic it was trying to go after.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

After spending another week with it, though, its unconventional look slowly grew on me — even if that appreciation is mostly isolated to the front of the EV. That’s due to Hyundai’s signature Parametric Pixel LED light bar, which stretches across the nose like something straight out of a sci-fi movie. Those individual blocks give it a retro look that becomes even more dazzling from dusk into the night. In a sea of generic crossovers, this one certainly commands road presence.

Sources indicate that that said, I still haven’t come to terms with the back half of this electric SUV. That tapered, upright rear end remains the hardest pill to swallow, giving it the look of a boat tail. Despite this, I now appreciate that the shape is doing the heavy lifting to make it aerodynamic — and subsequently boosting its efficiency.

According to recent reports, whether I’m making a quick stop at the local grocery store or on my 30+ mile commute to work, the 2026 Hyundai Ioniq 9 doesn’t skimp on the comforts. Step inside, and it’s clear Hyundai prioritized first-class comfort for the people riding up front and in the middle.

Industry observers note that for example, the plush H-Tex seats strike a great balance of softness and support — which, for the driver, includes extra pampering courtesy of Hyundai’s Ergo Motion seat. When activated, it slowly adjusts the firmness of the cushion, sort of like getting a mini massage while driving, all to deter fatigue on longer hauls.

Still, the real VIP treatment belongs to the second-row captain’s chairs. With both heating and ventilation, plus power-reclining backrests and extendable footrests, they turn the middle row into a rolling lounge. However, the third row leaves more to be desired. Although I still appreciate having the extra seating capacity in a pinch, the legroom back there is practically nonexistent for adults — so I’d much rather keep that rear bench folded flat to make way for more trunk space.

At nearly $80,000 as tested, the Ioniq 9 Calligraphy Design comes loaded with just about every luxury and tech perk anyone could ask for — and rightfully so.

Sources indicate that ​I still absolutely love Hyundai's adaptive cruise control, which makes long drives bearable and includes a dedicated lane-centering button on the steering wheel that also happens to work on local roads. Adding to that is a crisp Head-Up Display that projects my speed and navigation right onto the windshield.

​Changing lanes is effortless thanks to the Blind-Spot View Monitor (which streams a live camera feed straight into the digital gauge cluster) and a digital rearview mirror that offers a wider field of view than a conventional glass mirror.

​Back-seat passengers get plenty of love, too, with built-in rear side-window sunshades, a massive panoramic sunroof, and dazzling customizable ambient lighting that sets an upscale mood after dark.

​There’s also practical utility in the form of a handy 120V outlet accessible right in the trunk, letting me power laptops, tailgating gear, or small appliances straight off the SUV’s battery.

At nearly $80,000 as tested, the 2026 Hyundai Ioniq 9 Calligraphy Design is easily one of the most expensive vehicles in Hyundai’s entire lineup — and that price tag has long made me a skeptic.

Sources indicate that ​Yet spending a second week behind the wheel proved that judging it at face value is a mistake. Between its even better real-world efficiency, spacious cabin suited for families, and a laundry list of thoughtful luxury features, the Ioniq 9 delivers where it counts most: a family hauler that's rich in utility and backed by an efficient drive.

#16535. ‘Josephine’ Will Floor You

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1149 w)

‘Josephine’ Will Floor You

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1149 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollingstone

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This is the question that an eight-year-old named Josephine (Mason Reeves) asks her dad, Damien (Channing Tatum).
  • The cops arrest the perpetrator, the survivor goes to the hospital, and eventually, Damien is left with his daughter and that question, hanging in the air.
  • The Grand Jury Prize winner at this year’s Sundance Film Festival, Josephine doesn’t just follow its namesake as she’s forced to navigate a sudden loss of innocence; it sticks so closely to her perspective that you’re allowed to see every confusing gesture, every mixed-message reply, every argument among her parents, and every acting-out response through her eyes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This is the question that an eight-year-old named Josephine (Mason Reeves) asks her dad, Damien (Channing Tatum). She’s a sporty kid, the kind of youngster who accompanies her jockish pops on long runs through Golden Gate Park every Sunday morning. It’s during one of these weekly father-daughter bonding sessions that Josephine sprints ahead of her dad and strays off their usual path. Stopping to catch her breath, she sees a female jogger go into a public restroom at the bottom of a hill. Then Josephine watches as a stranger pulls the woman out, knocks her to the ground, and sexually assaults her.

The cops arrest the perpetrator, the survivor goes to the hospital, and eventually, Damien is left with his daughter and that question, hanging in the air. Josephine can’t comprehend what she’s witnessed. Her father doesn’t know how to answer. Instead of comforting or explaining, Damien just resumes their usual training exercises; he’s got to strengthen her up for soccer, he tells his daughter. His intentions are noble. He wants to protect her by pretending nothing’s happened. But Josephine’s father is simply the first adult who fails to help her process the traumatic experience this young girl has gone through. He won’t be the last.

The Grand Jury Prize winner at this year’s Sundance Film Festival, Josephine doesn’t just follow its namesake as she’s forced to navigate a sudden loss of innocence; it sticks so closely to her perspective that you’re allowed to see every confusing gesture, every mixed-message reply, every argument among her parents, and every acting-out response through her eyes. That itself isn’t unusual — most coming-of-age movies let you walk miles in their hero’s Converse All Stars. Yet writer-director Beth de Araújo’s sophomore film handles this shattering take on a kid wrapping her head around trauma with such grace, such delicacy, such force and a lack of false notes, that the work feels seismic even in its silences. It’s not interested in debating how crimes are handled by the cops or the courts, or how society talks around instead of about sexual violence in a constructive way. The movie wants you to reckon with the impact of someone figuring out a foreign landscape filled with unforeseen terrors. Josephine, c’est moi. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

So much of this rests on the tiny shoulders of Reeves, a first-time actor who seems to intuitively understand how to simply be in front of the camera. When Araújo isn’t replicating Josephine’s point of view, letting things unfold from a lower angle looking up or glimpsed from a distance, she’s training her lens directly on Reeves’ face in close-up. You can see the character attempting to grasp and contextualize situations for which she has no reference point in real time. And when Josephine begins to parrot statements and repeat patterns of behavior — she sees Damien spit on the rapist, then later spits on her dad in a fit of rage — we can see her trying on toxic versions of adulthood for size. It’s an incredible performance by any parameter, much less one delivered by a preteen.

Josephine makes space for her parents as well, with Tatum weaponizing his varsity-athlete physicality and kinder, gentler masculinity to play Damien as a well-meaning yet grasping dad, a paterfamilias in over his head when it comes to talking about tough subjects. His solutions: Take a self-defense class and either sweat out the pain or bury it. Gemma Chan plays Josephine’s mom, a dancer named Claire, as someone both more sympathetic to their child’s bewilderment and equally adrift. (A sequence in which she’s asked by her daughter if she’s ever been assaulted is all the more painful by the lack of an actual answer; Chan’s look alone tells you more than you feel you should know.) Tempers get lost, voices get raised, and Josephine herself lashes out in ways that suggest she doesn’t know how to deal with the emotional turbulence coursing through her. There’s a scene that takes place in a partially painted nursery that you may require you to cover your eyes. Trending Stories Marlon Jackson Reveals Stage 4 Prostate Cancer Diagnosis Selena Gomez Shares Her Reaction to Martin Short Ruining Her Wedding Cake Some Gamers Are Pissed That ‘GTA VI’ Makes Them Be Nice to Their Girlfriend Trump Got Played by Putin and Xi Related Content How a 1972 Cocktail Party Gave Us the Best Documentary of the Year Channing Tatum Says He Hasn’t Been Harassing Zoë Kravitz and Harry Styles With Burner Account ‘The Weight’ Isn’t a Perfect Homage to 1970s Tough-Guy Movies. But It’s Close ‘I Want Your Sex’ Works Out the Kinks of a BDSM Relationship.

Recent findings suggest that you don’t need to know that Josephine comes from an extremely personal place to feel that Araújo (whose debut, a Neo-Nazi Karen parable titled Soft and Quiet, now feels like an artist clearing her throat before speaking harshly and loudly) is unpacking this youngster’s story with an extraordinary amount of acuity and sensitivity, even as she refuses to pull punches: The assault is shown forensically, pitilessly, and in full. So is Josephine’s cross-examination on the stand by the defense’s lawyer (Dana Millican) when the child is forced to testify as a witness, which represents the ways our legal system can put everyone involved on trial. Surreal touches, such as the ghostly presence of the rapist (Philip Ettinger) hovering around everyday situations, add to the feeling that you’re viewing all of this through a highly subjective lens. Josephine sees this person everywhere, as a phantom both menacing and eerily childlike. So why shouldn’t we?

“Do you think the man is bad on the inside?” Josephine asks one of her caretakers. “Or good on the inside, but does bad things?” Nobody really knows the answer to that, she’s told. Neither Araújo nor the movie itself pretends to have a satisfying reply. But it’s desperate to ask the question and push you to wonder how a child, in some ways wise beyond her years yet still very much a kid, can reckon with a morality that exists in deepening shades of gray. Josephine is a movie that begins in a moment of fear — Josephine is scared to run out of her garage before the automatic door closes — and ends with a portrait of courage under fire. That the courage comes from someone who can barely comprehend her own bravery only makes the moment that much more impressive. It’s hard to think of a work of art that feels this simultaneously scarring and healing. Or that is tougher to watch yet something that must be seen as soon as possible and by any means necessary.

In a recent development, earlier this week, Apple revealed that Siri AI usage limits will be implemented in iOS 27.3 and explained how iCloud+ increases those limits. Now we have a real-world example of what it looks like when limits are hit, and details on what counts toward those limits.

Siri AI and select other AI features will begin having usage limits in iOS 27.3 for advanced tasks.

This is standard practice with other AI services like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude because these tools rely on server-based models rather than running entirely on-device.

Here’s an example from the iOS 27.3 beta showing what it looks like when you hit your Siri AI daily usage limit. Per Ben in a post on X:.

I hit my Siri AI usage limit, it still works though, including complex questions pic.twitter.com/XYYNPMnSnn.

In a follow-up post, Ben clarifies that complex questions did stop working shortly after posting. As expected though, basic requests continued to work as usual—they don’t have a usage limit.

One question that Apple hasn’t made clear is what qualifies as a complex or “advanced” Siri AI request. The company shares just two examples of something advanced:.

Suppose it gets it wrong like it does most of the time. I wonder if that still counts.

But leaker pdfu has discovered exactly the instructions Siri AI follows to determine whether a request counts as basic or advanced. In a post on X he outlines the parameters for requests deemed “advanced.”.

Siri AI will check the request against this list, and if it involves any of these, it’s deemed “advanced.”.

Sources indicate that it would be helpful if Apple publicly documented these guidelines for users. But perhaps after iOS 27.3 ships and usage limits are fully implemented, we’ll get more detail from the tech giant.

What do you think of Siri AI’s parameters for advanced requests in iOS 27.3? Let us know in the comments.

Over a year after D’Angelo’s death, the singer’s legacy lives on in Vice City thanks to an unreleased song that has appeared within the world of Grand Theft Auto 6.

GTA VI players uncovered the track — titled “Kamakazi,” as confirmed by D’Angelo collaborator DJ Dojah — on Worldwide FM, one of the many radio stations featured in the game; D’Angelo’s “Lady” also plays on the in-game Honey FM channel.

This is "Kamikaze," a previously unreleased D'Angelo song, that reportedly appears in the GTA VI radio station "Worldwide FM." pic.twitter.com/unZgAtCgRa.

D’Angelo’s music being posthumously immortalized in the most anticipated video game in a decade is a fitting tribute to the singer, given his previous collaborations with Rockstar Games, the firm behind GTA VI. Back in 2018, the usually reclusive D’Angelo contributed a fresh song titled “Unshaken” to Rockstar’s Red Dead Redemption 2.

According to recent reports, “[D’Angelo] would come in here [Rockstar’s Upcoming York city office] and just play the game. We weren’t even talking about doing music,” Ivan Pavlovich, Director of Music and Audio at Rockstar Games, told Rolling Stone at the time. “When D’Angelo comes through, he shows up at midnight, and he’s playing the game until four in the morning. Each time he was just like, ‘it’s incredible.’ It just blows his mind. He’s such a fan. I have never seen someone that excited.” Trending Stories Marlon Jackson Reveals Stage 4 Prostate Cancer Diagnosis Selena Gomez Shares Her Reaction to Martin Short Ruining Her Wedding Cake Some Gamers Are Pissed That ‘GTA VI’ Makes Them Be Nice to Their Girlfriend Trump Got Played by Putin and Xi.

It’s unclear whether “Kamakazi” was written and recorded specifically for GTA VI or if it was among the batch of unreleased music D’Angelo left behind following his death from pancreatic cancer in October 2025. Videos of “Kamakazi” uploaded onto YouTube have been hit with takedown notices from Sony Music Entertainment, which had D’Angelo signed to their RCA label.

In a recent development, in the year since his death, D’Angelo’s estate and collaborators have talked about the impending arrival of more unreleased music from the singer, including an entire LP’s worth of unheard music, a covers album, and a collection of B-sides. However, “Kamakazi” is the first taste of what remains in D’Angelo’s vaults.

According to recent reports, the changing of the clocks has taken its toll on my sleep this Fall. After long evenings bathed in artificial light, I've been feeling more wired than tired at bedtime. But thanks to one surprising gadget, lately I've been more consistent with my bedtime – and that's a good thing as studies link sleep consistency with better life expectancy.

Now that I’m prioritising a consistent sleep routine, I’m also waking up less through the night. So what is this surprising gadget? A red light face mask. Were you expecting something different? Mask aside, red light is stated to accentuate the production of sleep hormones.

However, sceptical that I’ve been lulling myself to sleep with nothing more than a placebo effect, I called on double-boarded sleep medicine specialist Dr. Chris Winter to ask whether the science around red lights sleep benefits checks out. Here's what he said...

Due to my job, I have a collection of gadgets to reach for when it comes to bedtime – the Ozlo Sleepbuds, Hatch Sleep Clock and the Oura Ring 5 included.

But one that's really surprised me lately is the Bob and Brad PhysioFace Light Therapy Mask, available for $169.99 (was $199.99) at Amazon.

I've been using the mask, chiefly marketed for skincare purposes, as part of my bedtime routine and it's helped me put down my phone and get to sleep on time.

It has been revealed that as much as I love my Hatch clock, I don't love that I have to use my phone to alter settings. That's the beauty of this red light mask – it’s independent from my phone (there's no app to download) with control buttons attached to the device itself.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

That means I am actually making my bedroom a phone-free space and instead focusing on winding down for a great night's sleep.

Recent findings suggest that it's hard to quantify exactly how well the red light mask is improving my sleep quality. But one thing is for sure: by the time I remove the mask, I feel sleepy and it never takes me long to dose off into a deep sleep.

According to my Garmin sleep timeline, I've reached deep sleep within half hour of dropping off, and continue to cycle through healthy sleep stages.

But what does Dr. Winter think? "It’s possible that taking a quiet break for your skincare routine is helping you unwind, particularly if it replaces scrolling or other stimulating activities.

"But feeling that you’re sleeping better doesn’t tell us whether the benefit is coming from the light itself, the routine, or something else.

"I would view it as a potentially relaxing part of your routine — not a proven sleep treatment," the board-certified neurologist cautions.

White and blue light from screens is bad news for sleep. But as the nights draw in, a lot of our evenings are powered by these types of light. This winter, I’ve been making a conscious effort to swap my overhead light for the sundown setting on my Hatch Sleep Clock. I've also been swapping doomscrolling with reading time while wearing my red light mask.

In a recent development, 20 minutes prior to bedtime – after writing my do-to list for the following day and shutting off my phone for the night – I pop the mask on in bed and start reading a book. The 10-minute timer on the mask ensures I read for at least 10 minutes before drifting off.

The mask has three light modes with different colored lights. I've been using the BOOST mode that combines red light and near-infrared light. As well as supposedly boosting skin health, red light is associated with relaxation and there is some science associating it with improved sleep quality.

Although evidence is limited, research by Chinese scientists published in the National Library of Medicine, suggests red light influences melatonin secretion, improving sleep initiation.

Industry observers note that dr. Winter also referred to a 2026 review of five randomized trials that found a modest improvement in self-reported sleep quality when red light was introduced. "But the authors emphasized that the evidence was limited and imprecise," he notes.

Industry observers note that additionally, red light face masks, like my Bob and Brad model, are built to increase collagen production. They do this by penetrating the skin with red light, which stimulates the cells responsible for collagen synthesis. Besides improving skin elasticity, collagen can also improve sleep. A 2024 study concluded that increasing collagen at bedtime reduces sleep fragmentation.

Placebo or not, the mask has helped me prioritise a consistent bedtime routine over the past two weeks, and sleep better than I was immediately after the clock change.

According to recent reports, I’ve been writing about sleep for over two years, and one thing I’ve learnt is that your sleep routine must be personal. A gadget or habit that works for someone else may not work for you.

If you’re struggling to sleep, you may need to try a few different methods or technologies before you hit on one that clicks. But one piece of advice sleep experts all agree on is that you need a relaxing prelude to sleep if you want to clock quality ZZZs.

A nighttime routine involves practising the same sequence of activities in the run up to your bedtime, helping prepare both your brain and body for sleep. In time, and with consistency, your body clock will come to recognise this routine as a signal to sleep, helping you drift off easily.

Industry observers note that dr. Winter explains: "A bedtime routine creates a predictable opportunity to step away from work, screens and other stimulating activities, rather than expecting your brain to switch off the moment your head hits the pillow. Pairing that wind-down period with a consistent sleep schedule and lower lighting helps support your body’s sleep-wake rhythm.".

This routine should be "simple, enjoyable and easy to repeat" and can include activity you find relaxing, be that a dark shower, mediation, reading, stretching or simply listening to calm music.

"You don’t need an elaborate checklist or expensive equipment—the goal is to wind down, not give yourself another assignment," advises the host of the Sleep Unplugged podcast.

"Think of the routine as making room for sleep, not forcing it to happen.".

I began working on dettato about 10 months ago, but scrapped what I had in about April. The reason why was that I treated AMT as a data problem - but in reality, the bottleneck is architecture. There are a lot of parellels that you can draw for OMR (first model i made) and AMT. both traditionally were tackled early on using algorithms. later, in both fields they plugged in giant LLM components. These models would naturally become overfit to synthetic data, since globally the problems of AMT and OMR become different than if you treat it locally. But, for both you can reframe it as a local problem. For OMR, using a detector model. For AMT, a pitch-lane model.

#16526. How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?

📅 06 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 15m • 📚 Deep Dive (2971 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ieee ↗ Open Full Page

How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (2971 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ieee

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.
  • Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.
  • Last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.

Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.

Last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun. Phobos, the Martian moon named for the Greek god of fear and panic, was transiting the solar disk. Too small to darken the pale, dust-tinged sky, but orbiting close enough to eclipse a significant fraction of the Sun, Phobos passed in less than a minute.

NASA’s Perseverance rover captured Phobos passing in front of the Sun from the surface of Mars.ASU/MSSS/SSI/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

In a recent development, the tiny moon, with its murky origins, is an enigma, and one whose makeup and history could tell us much about Mars and the wider solar system. And now the international Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission, which successfully launched on 20 October, seeks to explore that mystery with an unprecedented series of landings on the unknown surface of Phobos.

This mission brings unusual challenges—for example, designing an orbit to study a microgravity moon orbiting a much larger planet. Engineers also had to figure out how to assess and land on this low-gravity pile of loosely assembled dirt and rock, how a rover might rove across it, and how the spacecraft might take samples and return them to Earth.

“I often say that landing on Phobos is like trying to land a balloon,” says Yasuhiro Kawakatsu, project manager of MMX at the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). “It’s very difficult to drop a balloon to the ground and prevent it from tilting or bouncing.”.

It has been revealed that phobos is one of two small Martian moons; the other is Deimos, named after the Greek god of dread and terror. Their cosmic origins are unknown, though there are two prevailing theories. One holds that the moons were once asteroids from the belt between Mars and Jupiter, captured by the smaller planet’s gravity. In the other theory, Phobos and Deimos formed when a large celestial body slammed into Mars, sending debris into orbit. Some models suggest the pair are the last survivors from a cluster of satellites.

The enormous Stickney crater, roughly 9 kilometers across, dominates this view of Phobos taken by NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.University of Arizona/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

Industry observers note that scientifically speaking, Phobos is considered a rubble pile, a loosely consolidated aggregate of rock and dust. Far too small to become spherical under its own mass, it’s shaped like a lumpy potato, roughly 27 kilometers in length, with only 1/1,800th of Earth’s gravity. On Phobos, a typical adult would weigh about as much as a tennis ball does on Earth.

In a recent development, more than 10 years in the making, MMX released on Japan’s flagship H3 rocket from Tanegashima spaceport on 20 October local time. It will arrive at Mars in 2027 carrying scientific payloads from several space agencies, including NASA, and a upcoming rover called Idefix developed by the French and German space agencies (CNES and DLR) in collaboration with JAXA.

Engineers assembled MMX’s modules at Japan’s Tanegashima Space Center before the spacecraft’s October 2026 launch.JAXA.

MMX consists of three modules: a propulsion module to power its journey to Mars and apply the brakes to enter orbit around the red planet; an exploration module carrying the rover, sampling gear, and other scientific instruments; and a return module, attached to the exploration module, that harbors the capsule destined for a high-speed reentry into Earth’s atmosphere. After collecting samples on Phobos, the exploration and return modules will lift off together. The exploration module will then be jettisoned while the return module sets a course back home.

If all goes according to blueprint, MMX will deliver a 10-gram sample to Earth in the second half of 2031. But the mission will face a series of daunting challenges to reach that end point, including navigating complex orbits around Phobos and landing on its surface while Mars periodically blocks communications with Earth.

The MMX’s modular design includes the propulsion module [left] and the exploration and return modules [right].Kyodo News/Getty Images.

“It’s the most complex mission I have ever seen,” indicates Patrick Michel, director of research at CNRS (the French National Center for Scientific Research) and co-principal investigator on Idefix.

An H3 rocket carried MMX into space on 20 October 2026, beginning the mission’s five-year journey to Phobos and back.The Asahi Shimbun/Getty Images.

It has been revealed that once MMX reached low Earth orbit, its propulsion module’s engine fired, kicking off a nearly year-long deep-space cruise to Mars. On arrival, the spacecraft will need to fire its engines in an extended, carefully timed burn to slow down enough to be captured by Mars gravity. The propulsion module will then be jettisoned, leaving the exploration and return modules to orbit Mars.

“If something doesn’t go according to strategy, MMX will fly by Mars and get catapulted into the solar system,” says Nicola Baresi, an astrodynamicist who coauthored a paper on specially designed orbits for MMX.

It has been revealed that from that initial orbit, MMX will transition into a specially designed quasi-satellite orbit that allows it to keep pace with the small moon but also move around it. Since Phobos is too small to orbit in the conventional sense, the spacecraft will orbit Mars alongside the moon, following a clever egg-shaped path that slings MMX alternately ahead of and behind the moon. “When you’re closer to Mars, you’re accelerating with respect to Phobos, and when you’re farther from Mars, you’re decelerating. So you essentially go back and forth,” explains Baresi.

Martian Maneuvers To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.Chris Philpot.

To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.

The best existing images of Phobos, from spacecraft such as NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and ESA’s Mars Express, have resolutions of only a few meters per pixel. That’s larger than Idefix, the mission’s rover, itself about the size of a microwave oven. To map the surface in greater detail, MMX will loop in front of and behind Phobos at distances ranging from 200 kilometers to less than 20 km from the surface.

In a recent development, during its two-year remote sensing campaign, the exploration module will use several cameras and a laser altimeter to map the surface in high resolution and look for candidate landing sites. When Mars passes behind the Sun as seen from the Earth, causing a roughly two-week communications blackout, MMX will retreat into a larger, stable orbit. After communications resume, MMX will prepare to send its first visitor down to the surface.

Before the exploration and connected return modules attempt to land, Kawakatsu says, MMX will send a scout that in Japanese is called “the first penguin,” leaping into unknown waters. For this mission, the first to leap will be the Idefix rover, named for the canine companion to Obelix in the French comics series Asterix. The exploration module will release the rover during a low-altitude pass of between 40 and 100 meters above Phobos’s surface in 2028 or early 2029.

MMX will use its TENGOO camera [left] and LIDAR laser altimeter [right] to map Phobos’s terrain.JAXA.

According to recent reports, it will be a tense moment that calls back to 2005, during Japan’s Hayabusa mission to explore the asteroid Itokawa. In a similarly designed drop, the MINERVA rover was released from an orbiter, but erroneously at 200 meters instead of the intended 70 meters. The rover missed the asteroid and, without propulsion, drifted off into deep space.

Idefix will get a slight nudge out of the exploration module toward its negligible-gravity target, freefalling and likely tumbling as it goes. It’s expected to touch down with a velocity of less than 1 meter per second. Unlike rovers that have landed on other surfaces with airbags or dedicated landing legs, Idefix will land without protection, apart from some extra padding on the solar panels due to their critical nature. The barely-there gravity of Phobos should allow the 23-kilogram rover to land softly, though exactly how this landing will play out is hard to predict.

The Idefix rover will travel to Phobos with its wheels tucked in and solar panels folded.DLR.

According to recent reports, “It will bounce probably several times,” indicates Stephan Ulamec, Idefix’s co-principal investigator and project manager at DLR. “It will come to rest somehow in some position.” Once it’s still, four retracted legs will deploy to right the rover autonomously, regardless of its orientation. It will then unfold its solar panels to charge its batteries for exploration tasks ahead.

Sources indicate that A simulation shows how Idefix is expected to tumble onto Phobos, right itself using its articulated legs, and begin exploring the moon’s surface. DLR.

Recent findings suggest that once operational, Idefix will roll at a snail’s pace, topping out at one millimeter per second. Its metal wheels have protruding blades like a paddle wheel, designed to gain traction in Phobos’s microgravity. “If we were to drive our rover faster, then it would actually be more like we were swimming through instead of driving across the surface,” indicates Cecily Sunday, a doctoral student involved in testing Idefix’s WheelCams at the Institut Superieur de l’Aeronautique et de l’Espace (ISAE-Supaéro) in Toulouse, France.

The WheelCams, a pair of cameras placed on the underside of the rover, will observe the wheels and their tracks during Idefix’s planned 100-Earth-day primary mission. The images will help researchers study the size and distribution of grains in Phobos’s regolith and how cohesive they are. How much or how little the grains stick together will greatly impact how Idefix moves. Sunday likens this to the difference between driving on dry and wet sand. “Think of trying to build a sandcastle with dry sand,” she says. “You can’t. Add water, and suddenly you can.”.

The Idefix rover was mounted between the MMX spacecraft’s landing legs for the journey to Phobos.DLR.

The team tested the rover’s nine-bladed wheels on a variety of materials, including Phobos regolith simulants provided by JAXA and DLR, lunar simulants, glass beads, quartz sand, and clay pebbles. “We characterize the mechanical properties of each simulant precisely, then test across the full range, with varying grain size, angularity, and even color, so we can map what we see in the WheelCam images back to actual surface properties,” Sunday says.

In a recent development, despite the microgravity and Phobos’s rubble-pile nature, Sunday says Earth-based tests can approximate the rover’s motion on the surface of the small moon fairly well. While Phobos’s reduced gravity lowers the rover’s effective weight, there is also reduced pressure between the grains beneath its wheels. “As long as you’re moving very, very slowly and using the same materials and the same weight of the system, they should be representative,” Sunday says.

With four paddle-like wheels and deployable solar panels, Idefix is designed to crawl across Phobos.Ardan Fuessmann/Imago/Alamy.

According to recent reports, idefix’s interactions with its new home will offer “sub-millimeter resolution and information on porosity, on grain size, on surface strength, on how hard is the material,” Ulamec says. “It fills a gap between remote observations from orbit and detailed observations of the return samples back on Earth.”.

Sources indicate that what Idefix finds on this rocky, rugged world will help determine how and where JAXA attempts to land the main spacecraft. Michel says the touchdown will provide ground truth for understanding of Phobos. When NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft touched down on the asteroid Bennu to collect a sample, its sampling arm surprisingly sank nearly half a meter into the loose material. But Ulamec doesn’t think Idefix will sink deep into Phobos, noting that Bennu is very different and much smaller, with a diameter of 500 meters.

Once Idefix has investigated the surface, MMX will face an even greater challenge: landing its much larger exploration module on Phobos. The spacecraft will make a controlled descent to roughly 10 meters above the surface, then drop the remaining distance in free fall. With so little gravity to pull it downward, even a small sideways motion could cause the lander to tip or bounce away. A successful, upright landing would mark the start of up to two hours on Phobos for the crucial sampling phase.

According to recent reports, the MMX mission draws on the experience and technologies of Japan’s two Hayabusa sample-return missions, which landed on the asteroids Itokawa and Ryugu. But this mission has many more moving parts. MMX’s exploration module will use two sampling devices—a coring sampler developed by JAXA and a pneumatic sampler provided by NASA and fabricated by Honeybee Robotics, a subsidiary of Blue Origin. Data from these tools, and those carried by the Idefix rover, could answer questions about the origin of Phobos and how the Mars system has evolved.

The coring sampler uses a robot arm and a cylindrical corer designed to reach at least 2 centimeters below the surface. The arm can maneuver to find the best site for digging. “That by itself is a challenge because we’ve never done it,” Michel notes. “You never know what can happen at the very sampling site itself, where you might have a boulder and the arm cannot move.”.

According to recent reports, probing beneath the top layer will be valuable because solar radiation, galactic cosmic rays, and micrometeorites have battered and weathered the surface. The material below should offer a better record of the moon’s origins, and JAXA aims to collect at least 10 grams of it.

MMX will carry both the Idefix rover [bottom] and a robotic coring sampler [top] designed to dig beneath Phobos’s weathered surface.JAXA.

In a recent development, the pneumatic sampler takes a different approach. Mounted on one of the lander’s legs, it will inject pure, non-reactive nitrogen gas into the surface and capture the grains stirred up. This sample could illuminate the changes Mars and its moons have undergone over time. The dual system also adds redundancy in the face of Phobos’s unknowns. “If the surface of Phobos proves to be very hard, [the coring sampler] may struggle to penetrate the ground. [The pneumatic sampler] would not experience this matter and still be able to gather material,” Kawakatsu indicates.

Sources indicate that one of the most intriguing aspects of MMX is the additional possibility of collecting material from the planet below. It’s likely that Phobos has been peppered by Martian ejecta thrown into space by meteor impacts, so MMX also provides an opportunity to return the first Martian samples to Earth. Michel estimates that the samples could contain “a few hundred grains coming from Mars.” Scientists can distinguish those grains from native Phobos material by analyzing their oxygen isotopes.

That possibility raises a planetary-protection question. A direct Mars sample-return mission would have to follow strict rules to ensure that potentially living biological material from Mars doesn’t contaminate Earth. But those protocols don’t apply to MMX, even if its sample does collect grains of Martian soil. A panel of experts concluded that any microbes blasted off Mars wouldn’t survive the violent impact and ejection or the intense radiation exposure on the way to Phobos. This saved MMX from implementing expensive and time-consuming quarantine and containment protocols for the returning sample.

After landing on Phobos, MMX will have roughly two hours to collect samples from the moon’s surface before lifting off again.JAXA.

According to recent reports, during the brief surface operation, the robotic arm will deposit the samples in a storage unit, from which they’ll be transferred into a capsule aboard the return module and sealed in a vacuum. After that, lift off.

Once back in Mars orbit, the exploration module will resume its observations of Phobos and make several flybys of Mars’s other diminutive moon, Deimos, to gather data on its surface, structure, and composition. In November 2030, during a favorable alignment of Mars and Earth, MMX will begin the homeward leg of its trip. The return module will separate from the exploration module and power the voyage home, its sole objective to bring the dust of Phobos to Earth.

MMX’s sample return capsule will carry material from Phobos through Earth’s atmosphere in 2031.JAXA.

According to recent reports, finally, in 2031, the 60-centimeter-wide sample capsule will plunge into Earth’s atmosphere at roughly 12 kilometers per second. Assuming it survives the extreme heat of reentry and lands safely in Australia, scientists will begin to tease out clues about Phobos and the early solar system. JAXA’s Institute of Space and Astronautical Science will receive and curate the samples, which will also be shared with mission partners.

“We have macroscale measurements from the spacecraft, microscale measurements with the rover, and then sample analysis,” Michel notes. “So we can relate the three kinds of scales together because we have all of them.” The insights gleaned from orbital images, close-up images of the regolith, and the chemical analysis of the samples could have wider implications for our understanding of our solar system.

It has been revealed that “MMX is a mission to understand the Mars system and shed light onto how terrestrial planets like the Earth, and maybe Mars, develop a habitable environment,” Kawakatsu indicates. “We strongly suspect that our terrestrial planet region formed dry, and water and organics were scattered inwards from the icy-rich outer solar system.” Mars, he says, sits at the gateway between the inner and outer solar system, making its moons valuable witnesses to the processes that shaped potentially habitable worlds.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Holidays that revolve around doing a whole lot of cooking and hunting for gifts tend to be the most stressful.

For me, the week before Thanksgiving puts my brain into overdrive mode as I help my parents choose what we’re going to cook, write up a grocery shopping list and decide on who we’re inviting to dinner. The overwhelming sense of stress that kicks in during that November holiday pre-planning has driven me crazy for years. But since I’ve mastered my use of AI tools this year, I knew it was time to put it to the test to see how it could assist me and my parents with our annual “Turkey Day” preparation.

So I went ahead and asked ChatGPT to bust out a list of the best prompts that specifically cater to helping anyone have a much easier time setting up their Thanksgiving festivities.

Once the chatbot generated its prompts, I walked away with a valid collection of commands that you can try out for yourself if you need a digital helping hand during your Thanksgiving planning.

ChatGPT’s collection of generated pre- and post-Thanksgiving planning helper prompts centered on assisting with coordinating the actual dinner, food shopping and cooking.

Industry observers note that one of those prompts even targeted the act of supporting someone who needs ideas on how to get the most out of their Thanksgiving leftovers. ChatGPT doesn’t just have to be your everyday recipe generator for the major day—it can also play the part of your reliable Thanksgiving planning assistant from this year forward.

Here are the seven best ChatGPT prompts that are all about setting it up as your go-to Thanksgiving planner:.

The first prompt is essential since it can do a good job of turning such an overwhelming holiday into more manageable daily tasks that lead right into the big day itself.

The second prompt works best for people who want to save as much money as possible during their Thanksgiving grocery shopping. The third prompt sticks out for its ability to help you build a coordinated dinner menu that reduces the chances of wasted food and any unnecessary cooking. The fourth prompt should aid you in making sure the turkey, mashed potatoes and other key Thanksgiving items makes its way to the dinner table at just the right time.

The fifth prompt is best for assisting folks who are worried about their Thanksgiving dinner hosting duties and need some tips on how to navigate the holiday as a whole. The sixth prompt should go a long way toward helping someone lessen their repeat visits to the supermarket, since ChatGPT can highlight everything you need to buy ASAP.

And finally, the seventh prompt can showcase all the standout dishes you can make with your Thanksgiving dinner leftovers (I’m always prone to making my very own turkey sandwich that’s known in most circles as “The Gobbler”).

It has been revealed that it takes so much energy to dedicate to setting up your Thanksgiving dinner and making sure your home is properly set up to handle all your guests. AI tools like ChatGPT have become a boon for people who need an extra helping hand when it comes to planning, so it makes sense that you can tap into them to make your Thanksgiving preparation less stressful.

Keeping any of these prompts for the years ahead, after seeing how efficient they can be at organizing this year’s Thanksgiving festivities, could be the move to make.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, for Warren, listening to music in the car holds sentimental meaning.
  • According to recent reports, “My only memory of music growing up was getting in the car and listening to my dad’s CDs, and John Mayer was his guy,” Warren said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that for country chart-topper Megan Moroney and pop hitmaker Alex Warren, a song isn’t necessarily finished when it leaves the studio. Sometimes, it needs a test drive.

In a recent development, for Warren, listening to music in the car holds sentimental meaning. On his latest album, Wildchild, he pays tribute to his late father, who died of cancer when Warren was just nine years old. Some of his most powerful musical memories with his dad are inseparable from time spent in the car.

According to recent reports, “My only memory of music growing up was getting in the car and listening to my dad’s CDs, and John Mayer was his guy,” Warren said. “When my dad passed away, I got in his car and [Mayer’s album] came on. When I wrote this song for my dad called ‘Wildchild,’ I put his voice on it, and I asked [Mayer] to do a guitar solo on it, so my dad and John have a song.”.

It has been revealed that the car is also where Warren discovered Moroney’s music. He recalls listening to her breakout hit “Tennessee Orange” in the car with his wife, who knew every word.

“She knows that song like the back of her hand, and it’s really cool because she applies it to her own life,” Warren remarked of Moroney’s autobiographical debut, which tells the story of a die-hard Georgia football fan falling for a Tennessee Volunteers fan.

“It encapsulates the kind of music my fans like,” noted Moroney, whose sharp-eyed songwriting turns specific details into universal feelings that resonate with the masses.

“It’s creative, it’s honest, there’s the hook, and it’s storytelling. I feel like at the root of all of my songs, that’s what it is. And obviously I’m a Georgia Bulldog, so it’s just very me.”.

Moroney and Warren may come from different corners of the music world, but the two found plenty of common ground during a conversation outside Fox & Locke, a storied live-music venue tucked into the rolling countryside of Leiper’s Fork, Tennessee. The discussion was part of Rolling Stone’s Musicians on Musicians series. This time, Lexus sought to connect two artists from different backgrounds in an entirely new way by trading the usual lounge-like venues that host Musicians on Musicians conversations for the lounge-inspired quiet cabin of an all-electric 2027 Lexus TZ, which will make its debut this winter. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

As the conversation continued, Moroney and Warren learned that their paths to stardom have more than a few parallels. Both got an early boost from TikTok before breaking through with massive singles from their debut albums — Moroney with her five-times-platinum “Tennessee Orange,” Warren with his record-breaking “Ordinary.” Both have crossed genre lines through collaborations, and both released hit albums this year: Moroney’s autobiographical Cloud 9 and Warren’s deeply personal Wildchild. They also share a belief in one essential part of the creative process: the all-notable “car test.”.

For Warren, that test played a pivotal role in one of the biggest songs of his career. After receiving an early, stripped-down version of “Ordinary” — little more than his voice and a piano — he played it for his wife while they were driving. Her reaction told him everything he needed to know. “She was like, ‘I want more of it!’”.

The experience changed the way he shares fresh music. “Now I only show people songs in my car.”.

He might be onto something. Whether you’re a professional musician or more of a carpool-karaoke type, there’s something about hearing a song on the road that changes the experience. A lyric lands a little harder. A melody feels a little bigger. And sometimes, the right song at the right moment can turn a daily drive into something worth remembering. It helps when the sound system is up to the task. The all-electric Lexus TZ features an available 21-speaker Mark Levinson audio system, engineered specifically for the TZ’s three-row cabin to deliver the kind of rich, immersive sound that feels the way it was meant to be heard.

Of course, when your life revolves around music, sometimes the best soundtrack is no soundtrack at all. For artists like Moroney and Warren, who spend much of their time on the road, a long drive can also offer a rare chance to unplug, catch up, and simply have a conversation. The TZ makes room for both experiences, and that balance between sound and silence feels particularly fitting for two artists who know a song’s power to make a personal story resonate far beyond its original inspiration.

It’s a reminder that the songs we carry with us are rarely just about the music. They’re tied to people, places, and moments that stick around long after the last note fades. And sometimes, the best way to know whether a song really works is to get behind the wheel, turn it up, and see where it takes you.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the Guardian reports that three US senators have sent letters to the CEOs of Apple, Google, and Meta, demanding answers about their failure to prevent access to AI-powered ‘nudify’ apps.
  • Last month, Apple updated its App Store rules in an attempt to crack down on apps that enable owners to generate nonconsensual nude images.
  • According to the updated rules, apps that allow users to create AI-generated content must include safeguards against abuse, including tools to filter objectionable material, report offensive content, and block abusive users.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the Guardian reports that three US senators have sent letters to the CEOs of Apple, Google, and Meta, demanding answers about their failure to prevent access to AI-powered ‘nudify’ apps. Here are the details.

Last month, Apple updated its App Store rules in an attempt to crack down on apps that enable owners to generate nonconsensual nude images.

According to the updated rules, apps that allow users to create AI-generated content must include safeguards against abuse, including tools to filter objectionable material, report offensive content, and block abusive users.

Apple also warns that apps used primarily for pornographic content or the objectification of real people may be removed from the App Store without notice.

While definitely well-intended, Apple’s changes came amid growing reports of AI-powered nudify apps, which easily allow users to generate nonconsensual intimate images.

Two months before these changes, Apple removed an app that allowed users to create pornographic deepfakes of real people after WIRED reached out for comment, which in turn came one month after San Francisco City Attorney David Chiu demanded that Apple and Google remove several nudify apps from their app stores.

Apple also removed several apps following investigations by the Tech Transparency Project (TTP), which published reports in January and April revealing that such apps were widely available on the App Store, sometimes even appearing in sponsored search results.

Throughout these investigations, Apple has maintained that nudify apps have always been prohibited under its App Review Guidelines, and that it proactively rejects and removes apps that violate its policies, including those flagged through user reports.

Apple, of course, is not alone in this challenge, with Google facing similar criticism over their availability on the Play Store, and Meta coming under scrutiny for allowing developers to advertise these apps on Facebook and Instagram, as highlighted in the WIRED report mentioned above.

Which brings us to today’s report from The Guardian.

According to The Guardian’s exclusive report, “three Senate Democrats sent letters to tech CEOs saying safeguards against nudification apps are insufficient on their platforms.”.

According to recent reports, A trio of US Senators say Apple and Google are failing to effectively detect and remove apps that can be used to generate nonconsensual nude or pornographic imagery. They also say Meta is continuing to profit off of ads for these so-called nudification apps that “victimize women and girls worldwide”.

The senators, namely Ron Wyden of Oregon, Ed Markey of Massachusetts, and Ben Luján of New Mexico, claim that in addition to failing to remove these apps, the companies may actually be profiting from their distribution and promotion.

Commenting on the letter, both Google and Meta said they prohibit such apps or their promotion and work to detect and remove violations from their platforms, broadly echoing what Apple has repeatedly stated when reached for comment in the past over these same concerns.

However, Wyden’s office argues that simply reaffirming, or in Apple’s case, updating these policies, means little if the companies continue to struggle to enforce them.

It has been revealed that keith Chu, the chief communications adviser and deputy policy director to Wyden, said that clarifying policies is not the same thing as enforcing them. Despite the companies reaffirming the prohibition of these apps, they continue to proliferate across Apple and Google app stores or be promoted in ads on Meta platforms, he added.

In its latest investigation, published just last month, TTP found 135 apps capable of generating nude or pornographic imagery on the App Store and the Play Store, using accounts registered to 13-year-old boys.

Additionally, researchers found that even accounts configured with parental controls were able to download these apps without requiring parental approval.

Despite Apple and Google removing the apps identified in the investigation, The Guardian noted that these apps continued to work on devices where they had already been installed.

Now, Senator Wyden warns that Congress may need to step in if the companies fail to do a better job of cracking down on these apps.

To read The Guardian’s full report, follow this link.

Upgrade, 8:40 p.m. ET: In a statement to 9to5Mac, Apple remarked:.

Industry observers note that “We designed the App Store to be a safe and trusted place for consumers. A number of the apps in the TTP report are mainstream photo and video editing tools with legitimate, widely used functionality, and do not have nudification or deepfake capabilities. We prohibit nudify apps on the App Store, and remove developers who add capabilities like it after the App Review process — a malicious tactic known as bait-and-switch. We previously removed 28 of the apps referenced in this report before it was shared with us and have taken action on the remaining apps found to violate our rules. The report also relies on testing from older software that does not reflect current Apple safety features, including expanded protections for teens and parental controls in Screen Time that give families the ability to block kids and teens from downloading apps rated above their age.”.

Expanding on the safety features mentioned in its statement, Apple noted that teens aged 13 through 17 now have certain protections enabled by default, including web content filters, even if their parents haven’t configured any restrictions, and pointed to ⁠this support article for more information.

The tech giant added that children under 13 are required to use Child Accounts, and that the report relied on its previous 17+ age rating system, which was replaced last year with a more granular system that includes 13+, 16+, and 18+ ratings.

Just curious. Why doesn't someone from Apple try out the app before approving it, rather than approving it and waiting until people complain? I know there are many thousands of apps on the App store. But given that Apple makes money off most of these apps, it could surely afford to hire a staff charged with reviewing submitted apps to ensure compliance with the App store's guidelines and requirements before making them available in the App store. What am I missing here?

Apple also noted that in its report, TTP counted apps depicting people in swimwear or lingerie, which the organization said does not constitute nudification or, in itself, violate its guidelines.

Recent findings suggest that as for parental controls, Apple explained that, although apps that exceed a child’s configured age restrictions won’t appear in curated App Store sections, they can still be found through search, allowing children to request permission to download them through Ask to Buy. Without parental approval, the download remains blocked.

Apple added that Ask to Buy is supposed to require parental approval even for purchases made using gift card balances, including subscriptions. The organization remarked that if a purchase didn’t trigger an approval request, that would be unexpected behavior, and that it is investigating further.

Sources indicate that revision, November 19, 4:00 p.m. ET: In response to Apple’s statement, TTP director Katie Paul reached out to 9to5Mac with the following comment:.

Apple’s statement on nudify apps sidesteps vital problems and leaves out key context. The company claims it prohibits nudify apps but doesn’t address how its age rating system for apps contributes to the problem. TTP has shown how Apple relies on information provided by app developers to set age ratings—a self-reporting system that allows many nudify and pornographic apps to be misleadingly labeled a suitable for minors. Apple also continues to talk about removing nudify apps from the App Store, without mentioning that apps that are “removed” continue to be fully functional on people’s phones.

There are many questions about Apple’s policy on nudify apps that the statement fails to address. Apple has adopted a limited definition of “nudify.” The manufacturer defines nudify apps as capable of showing someone naked, not stripping them down to a bikini or lingerie. But the company also indicates it bans “creepy” and “nonconsensual intimate imagery.” What if an app is used to depict a woman in a bikini without her consent? We have asked Apple to clarify that and have not heard back.

In a recent development, as for Apple’s comment that TTP relied on “older software,” that may refer to the fact that Apple rolled out fresh child safety features in the fall. Our research was conducted in summer 2026. But many of Apple’s new features pertain to parent-supervised accounts on Apple, which have to be set up by a parent. Apple relies entirely on parents to go out of their way to locate and enable these settings. This raises obvious questions about how many people actually do this.

Breaking: Running two PSP emulators on one Switch 2 and sharing one via GameShare

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This branch experiments with a separate PPSSPP guest running on the host Switch 2 and streamed to a stock GameShare client.
  • It has been revealed that the working single-instance checkpoint is switch2-single-instance-working (commit 1c3b38a).
  • According to recent reports, open FTPD for the second command.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This branch experiments with a separate PPSSPP guest running on the host Switch 2 and streamed to a stock GameShare client. It is not a mirrored controller or a second PSP controller in the host emulator. Compilation and host tests do not establish console operation or acceptable two-game performance.

It has been revealed that the working single-instance checkpoint is switch2-single-instance-working (commit 1c3b38a). Its exact tested NRO, package and matching debug ELF remain under dist-switch2/checkpoints/switch2-single-instance-working/.

According to recent reports, open FTPD for the second command. A successful transfer is accepted without a validation download. The experiment installs as PPSSPP GameShare, at sdmc:/switch/ppsspp-switch2-gameshare/ppsspp-switch2-gameshare.nro. It leaves the working ppsspp-switch2 NRO and its settings/saves in place. The normal Tools/build-switch2.sh selects GameShare OFF. Both builds reuse the build cache, but packaging rejects mismatched native/experimental modes.

It has been revealed that launch through the same GameShare-capable native title override used for the Moonlight SDK example. A generic title override is not known to grant the required GameShare context. If another title locks profile switching, the SDK uses the Nintendo profile selected for that launch when available. The host log distinguishes a missing launch profile from a later StreamPlay or matchmaking error. Choose GameShare (experimental) in the host's main or pause menu, then join from the client's system GameShare screen. The client should see its own PPSSPP menu, with a guest-only startup message, and browse sdmc:/switch/ppsspp-switch2/games. Both browsers can access SD-card games; no game files are copied into the package.

According to recent reports, choose the same GameShare action to stop sharing. The guest pauses between sessions, retaining its independent emulator state. Exiting the guest's PPSSPP ends that guest instance; restart the application before creating another. Exit the host normally when done. If a real cleanup failure reports retained resources, close the entire hosting title from HOME, rather than returning to hbmenu. The SDK explicitly requires this for uncertain native ownership.

Recent findings suggest that the build links a second PPSSPP frontend/core into a relocatable object and renames every defined core-owned global symbol and ELF COMDAT group signature. Only eight plain-data C entry points are exported. The audit requires distinct Config, memory-base and core-state symbols; the host also compares their runtime addresses before starting. SDK/OS/C++ runtime entry points remain shared. The two emulators have independent core, UI, filesystem state, JIT registries, Vulkan contexts and settings/memory-stick directories. They share one OS process, so a fatal error in either copy can still affect the entire app.

According to recent reports, the host keeps its 1920x1080 output and 120 Hz request. The guest uses PPSSPP's existing offscreen Vulkan path at 1280x720 with a 60 fps presentation target. A readback callback transfers completed RGBA frames to a latest-frame mailbox; a dedicated presenter uploads them to a separate native VI2 guest layer. This first route adds CPU readback/swizzle cost; zero-copy is not claimed.

Sources indicate that the GameShare SDK is vendored from Moonlight-Switch's research worktree. Switch/GameShare/sdk-provenance.json records the source revision and file hashes. Its MIT license and per-file ISC notices are retained. The SDK's pinned CPU-console uploader is disabled. The guest renderer borrows the statically linked OunceVK driver's GSV main and worker sessions and uses its registered VM. It owns the guest image backing, registrations and client. The adapter tracks the driver's occupied slots at the libounce call boundary and reserves a free slot for guest range retirement. Each GameShare session reuses the reserved slot's completion event, which closes with the Vulkan driver's GPU. It does not access OunceVK's internal structs. Retire the guest images before Vulkan teardown. Coexistence and reuse on hardware still require qualification.

Sources indicate that the SDK owns matchmaking, native hosting, controller reads and the separate VI2 display/layer. Renderer retirement runs before native Finalize; layer closure runs afterwards. Uncertain presentation or release/retirement failure retains backing and blocks ordinary unload. Guest controls never enter the host emulator. Stale/disconnected snapshots become neutral.

Recent findings suggest that host settings/saves use ppsspp-switch2-gameshare/config/ppsspp; guest settings/saves use ppsspp-switch2-gameshare/guest/config/ppsspp. The existing working app's memory stick is not reused. Guest native text-entry applets are disabled because their routing to the remote screen is not implemented.

In a recent development, PPSSPP sends the guest emulator's PCM to the native per-guest queue and keeps the host emulator on normal AudOut. See the recovered audio contract. The console test confirmed audible client playback in the direct-audio build.

Sources indicate that start GameShare and join from the client. Open the same game on both screens, then enter its local wireless or Ad Hoc mode. Create a lobby on either console and look for it on the other. If the host had already initialized multiplayer before pairing, restart that game once to select the local route.

It has been revealed that while GameShare is hosting, PPSSPP runs its built-in discovery service and aemu_postoffice packet relay on IPv4 loopback ports 27314 and 27315. Both cores use the private route automatically with their existing, independently configured PSP MAC addresses. The guest still runs on the host Switch 2, so game packets stay on that console. The route does not use a public relay, Wi-Fi IP address, or UPnP mapping, and it does not change either core's saved network settings. Stopping GameShare closes the listeners. A game already in a lobby may need to leave and re-enter multiplayer after GameShare is restarted.

The user reported a successful Tekken session in the first loopback build. The subsequent build keeps each core's original MAC address and passed the ten paired desktop tests. That save-preserving version is tagged switch2-gameshare-multiplayer-baseline (commit 0699365). Its NRO, ZIP and debug ELF are in dist-switch2-gameshare/checkpoints/multiplayer-baseline/. The earlier console run used the temporary-MAC build.

Host boot.log, ppsspp.log, native-exit.bin and native-fault.bin live in the experimental app directory. The guest writes guest/ppsspp.log. Native fault/exit records with valid headers are retained as .previous on the next launch. Preserve diagnostics before relaunching after a failure.

Actual-source sanitizer tests cover native guest-image sector locations, partial creation, successful retirement, retained uncertain presents and release/range timeouts. SDK tests cover native lifecycle/cancellation, controller parsing/freshness and display ownership. They do not simulate the GPU, native title permissions, GameShare radio behavior or console performance. CPU, GPU, threading and shutdown regression risks require console testing; serialized PSP state layouts are unchanged.

It has been revealed that the dual-core AArch64 NRO and ZIP built and validated. The symbol audit found 27,173 renamed core-owned symbols and eight guest ABI exports. All 28 SDK native lifecycle scenarios, the input parser/freshness suite and display lifetime suite passed under ASan/UBSan. Six actual-source image-owner scenarios passed (clean, partial create, uncertain present, release timeout, range retirement timeout and unregister failure). Existing JIT publication and dedicated-worker tests also passed.

Sources indicate that host regression suites: 102 C++ unit tests passed; 527 executed single-instance PSP cases and ten paired relay scenarios passed. Eleven paired P2P cases remain unrun for the existing missing 127.0.0.2 host loopback alias, causing the aggregate runner's failure status. No executed regression test failed. Console dual-instance rendering, pairing, guest controls/audio and sustained performance still require physical qualification.

Recent findings suggest that the initial experimental build produced a system error before the PPSSPP menu. Its boot log reached display configuration; native fault/exit records remained empty. The separate working single-instance installation is unchanged. Pairing and the second emulator have not yet been reached on the console.

The SDK bridge is compiled as C++20 separately from the C++17 frontend. Startup checkpoints around Vulkan initialization write startup-stage.bin directly with native flushes. Its four little-endian 64-bit words are magic 0x3254475350505350, stage number, recorder address and system tick. Stages 1–4 cover diagnostics, display configuration, graphics-object construction and error-string construction; stages 10 and 11 bracket InitAPI's initial string assignment. Stages 20 and 21 bracket NativeInit, and 22 precedes window setup. The diagnostic boot marker is comdat-isolation. The native exit recorder also wraps svcBreak (kind 6, reason in the high 32 bits and a readable four-byte detail in the low 32 bits).

The final ELF highlighted that the linker turned a required host string-constructor call into a no-op. GCC used a local C5 signature for the constructor group. Renaming only global symbols let the guest group retain that signature, causing the linker to discard the host copy. The build now renames and checks all 7,351 guest COMDAT groups in addition to the global symbol audit. Disassembly of the corrected ELF confirms that host startup calls its own string constructor and the guest constructor has a distinct address.

The console opened the corrected build and started a host game. On the first GameShare attempt, VI2 reached the renderer hook, where a second GSV GPU open failed with 0x200F3. The guest emulator independently reached offscreen Vulkan initialization. The revised uploader uses the existing driver session. The host also joins the SDK thread after terminal states before asking if native resources were retained, so a completed thread alone no longer forces a title restart. Confirm pairing, guest frames and stop/restart on hardware.

Industry observers note that the shared-session build paired with the client, and the SDK completed cleanup. The client remained black because PPSSPP rejected readback from the guest's offscreen Vulkan presentation before any frame could reach the uploader. Offscreen presentation now declares its transfer-source capability. The copy waits for the color attachment writes and skips frames without an acquired image. A local MoltenVK run cleared three consecutive offscreen frames to different colors and verified every returned RGBA byte. Client presentation and independent input still require a console check.

It has been revealed that the console confirmed that the host and client can see and control their own PPSSPP screens. Both emulator audio streams were audible from the host. The console-confirmed NRO, matching ELF and installation receipt are saved under dist-switch2-gameshare/checkpoints/dual-screen-controls/.

Recent findings suggest that the client was silent in separate-display sessions with both AudOut and Audren. The Audren test boot log confirms the application mix used Audren, the guest received frames and SDK cleanup completed. The launcher NRO was restored to the console-confirmed dual-screen build using the saved SD-card copy. The renderer trial is recorded in commit c5a8716.

At the dual-screen checkpoint, both games played through the host. The SDK exposed an application-wide mirroring flag and device-volume configuration.

Industry observers note that the shipped SDK exports a separate PCM writer and per-guest queue counters. The reusable Moonlight SDK and its PPSSPP copy now expose a PCM callback. Tests of the native worker cover the recovered command layout, the unwritten tail after a partial write, and a failed audio command that leaves video and input running.

On November 19, 2026, the console test confirmed sound on the GameShare client. The working build is tagged switch2-gameshare-guest-audio-working (commit 50cd977). The exact installed NRO, SD-card package, matching ELF, SDK archive and build records are saved under dist-switch2-gameshare/checkpoints/guest-audio-working/. For a console rollback, reinstall that NRO as /switch/ppsspp-switch2-gameshare/ppsspp-switch2-gameshare.nro.
